blindSummary:
This state/province, anchored by the country's largest city, is the institutional counterweight to the anti-LGBT municipal-resolution movement that spread across more conservative parts of the country. In February 2024 the state/province's administrative court repealed the last remaining "against LGBT ideology" local resolution document. The organised response to those resolutions began here: in February 2019 the mayor of the country's largest city signed a 12-point municipal LGBT+ declaration (covering security, education, culture, sport and employment, drawn up with LGBT NGOs, and including an intervention hostel for homeless queer young people plus school "lighthouse keeper" support projects), and it provoked the first anti-LGBT municipal resolution in another town (March 2019) as an explicit counter-reaction. The state/province's administrative court system later carried out the annulment work that dismantled the resolution network nationally.

The unit's dark stain is historical: in November 2005 the then-mayor of the largest city banned its equality pride march, and a 2007 ruling by the regional human-rights court held that the ban violated assembly, effective-remedy and non-discrimination guarantees. That was 20 years ago and has not been repeated; the current institutional trajectory is clearly positive.

Institutionally this state/province stands above the national baseline — the only profiled unit described as doing so — because the court-repeal work and declaration infrastructure are concentrated here, while elsewhere the resolution legacy dominates and no equivalent mechanism exists.
